description: Developing Monitoring Programs for Protected Lands in Alaska is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NPS, U.S. National Park Service; NPS Arctic Inventory & Monitoring Network. Coastal habitats and archeological sites in western Alaska are at risk from coastal erosion. Researchers are documenting current assets and vulnerabilities for use in management decisions. Coverage: Alaska (2015). The toolkit gives Alaska as the location, 2015 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: Two large tracts of protected land along Alaska’s west coast face increasing threats from climate change. On the Seward Peninsula, the Bering Land Bridge National Preserve is a remnant of the land that once connected Asia with North America. The area is protected for the study of past cultures and to support the traditional lifestyles of current and future residents....
